title: PTC patches critical Windchill and FlexPLM vulnerability enabling remote code execution
summary: PTC released security patches for a critical CVSS 9.2 flaw in Windchill and FlexPLM software that allows unauthenticated remote code execution.

summary: A critical flaw in Red Hat Quay could allow attackers to steal private container images, overwrite repositories, and maintain persistent access.

summary: Node.js released fixes for 16 security flaws, including HTTP/2 bugs that allow unauthenticated clients to crash servers and leak sensitive data from other connections.

title: Microsoft Researchers Demonstrate AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
summary: Microsoft researchers demonstrated that AI agents can be backdoored by editing fewer than 10 neurons in open-weight models without retraining. The technique, called Lazarus, enables malicious command execution when triggered by specific strings.
takeaways: Nemotron-Terminal-8B: 7 neurons edited (98.8% success rate with 23 training sessions)
Qwen3.6-27B: 6 neurons edited (51-99.5% success rates)
Gemma-4-31B-IT: 99.5% success rates
Requires access to model checkpoint file before deployment; no threat actors observed using technique
Nemotron-Terminal-8B: 7 neurons edited, 98.8% success rate, 23 training sessions
Technique works on Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT models

No threat actors observed using technique in the wild

title: Iran-backed network directed attacks on Jewish and American sites across Europe and US
summary: US prosecutors unsealed an indictment on November 11, 2026, accusing three men of orchestrating attacks on Jewish and American sites across Europe on behalf of Iran's IRGC. The campaign included arson, stabbings, and a plot targeting RAF Fairford, with live-streamed attacks coordinated via FaceTime.
takeaways: Three defendants: Mohammad al-Saadi (Kataib Hezbollah), Mohsen Mohajeri (IRGC), Mohammed Ali al-Hassani (Iraqi national)
Targets: synagogues in Belgium/Netherlands/London, U.S. bank buildings in Amsterdam/Paris, RAF Fairford
~18 attacks/attempted attacks between March–April 2026

Campaign began days after U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran

title: Critical Zoom Workplace vulnerability allows unauthenticated privilege escalation
summary: Zoom released patches for two critical Workplace for Windows vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-108186 (CVSS 9.6) enabling unauthenticated remote privilege escalation, and CVE-2026-108187 (CVSS 8.1) enabling unauthenticated privilege escalation via network access. No in-the-wild exploitation reported.
takeaways: CVE-2026-108186: CVSS 9.6, affects versions 7.1.0–7.1.7, fixed in 7.1.8
CVE-2026-108187: CVSS 8.1, affects versions before 7.1.5
Both allow unauthenticated remote privilege escalation
No in-the-wild exploitation reported

title: Critical authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra exploited in active attacks
summary: A critical authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited to gain administrator access and compromise XCP-ng nodes. The flaw improperly converts authentication tokens to empty objects, allowing attackers to reuse valid tokens and achieve root-level XCP-ng takeover.
takeaways: Affects Xen Orchestra versions before 6.9.2 (stable) and 6.10.1 (latest)
Authentication token converted to empty object {}, returns first token in collection
Exploitation enables arbitrary code execution and full XCP-ng node takeover as root
Threat actor confirmed exploiting alongside zero-day requiring admin privileges
Unauthorized access not logged; no CVE assigned

title: Palo Alto Networks patches critical PAN-OS RCE vulnerability under active exploitation
summary: Palo Alto Networks released security updates for CVE-2026-0322, a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability in PAN-OS management interface currently under active exploitation.
takeaways: CVE-2026-0322 CVSS 8.6; authenticated RCE in PAN-OS management interface
Affects PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls and Panorama; Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access not affected
Very limited active exploitation; 3 U.S. IP addresses linked to attempts

title: NGINX releases patches for five vulnerabilities including critical RCE and TLS bug
summary: NGINX released patches on October 14 in versions 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 addressing five vulnerabilities, including three critical memory bugs rated 9.2 on CVSS v4.0 that could crash worker processes or enable remote code execution, plus a TLS client-certificate verification flaw rated 8.3.
takeaways: Three critical memory bugs rated 9.2 on CVSS v4.0 could crash workers or enable RCE
TLS vulnerability (8.3 CVSS) present since version 1.23.2 (October 2022) affects shared session caches
Fifth HTTP/3 flaw (6.9 CVSS) allows clients to inject extra bytes into backend requests
All vulnerabilities require specific configuration directives to expose
No active attacks reported as of October 15; none in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog

summary: Attackers exploited Fortinet vulnerabilities to install PEERSTITCH, a stealthy ARM64 malware on FortiGate firewalls in a telecom organization breach. Intrusion tracked as cluster CL-STA-0954 (aka UNC5820)

takeaways: CVE-2026-108097 rated 19/25 on Drupal risk scale enabling unauthenticated RCE

title: AI-Discovered Linux Kernel Vulnerability Allows Local Root Access and VM Escape
summary: A critical Linux kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-74580, 'Vghost') discovered by AI analysis allows local users to escalate privileges to root across nearly a decade of kernel versions (4.11–7.2-rc4). In certain virtualization setups, untrusted guest VMs can escape to the host hypervisor. The flaw ste
takeaways: Vghost affects Linux 4.11 through 7.2-rc4—nearly 10 years of releases
Allows local root escalation and potential VM-to-host escape in specific configurations
Root cause: vhost fails to invalidate cached memory mappings when ring reconfigured
Flaw originated 2017 (cache added), compounded 2020 (bounds check removed)
Tencent published proof-of-concept October 12; Ubuntu, RHEL, Amazon Linux, Azure Linux, Oracle Linux vulnerable; world-readable vhost device on 4 of 5 distros tested

takeaways: CVE-2026-105740 CVSS 9.9; authenticated RCE in Langflow <1.9.0

takeaways: 22 security notes released October 14; 4 critical vulnerabilities patched

summary: Doyensec researchers executed arbitrary code inside a Windows VBS enclave protecting SmartScreen using a four-byte write flaw and timing side-channel attack. takeaways: Four-byte write flaw in SFAPE.dll Initialize function; timing side-channel in second function

title: CISA warns of actively exploited Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day vulnerability
